exercises.why: Я не могу перевести этого слова. — DLI, Lesson 79.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: Tom doesn't seem to be leaving.
exercises.context: Я не могу перевести этого слова.

exercises.why: The verb **написать** is called perfective and expresses a single action with emphasis on its completion (either in the past or in the future, since the present tense deals only with actions in progress). — From the DLI Grammar Reference Book, Lesson 37.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: The verb **написать** is called perfective and expresses a single action with emphasis on its completion (either in the past or in the future, since the present tense deals only with actions in progress).

exercises.why: The imperfective aspect emphasizes the action itself. — From the DLI Grammar Reference Book, Lesson 37.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: The imperfective aspect emphasizes the action itself.

exercises.why: **сойти / сходить** — to go down, to come down, to descend, to get off; (figuratively) to come off, to disappear, to go from; to pass by; (figuratively) to pass for, to be taken for. **обойтись / обходиться** — to go around, to bypass (to pass by going around); to walk through, to wander around, to go around, to tour, to go to (many places in an area); to overtake, to outrank, to beat, to outperform (a peer or competitor). — DLI, Lesson 79.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: сойти / сходить — to go down, to come down, to descend, to get off; (figuratively) to come off, to disappear, to go from; to pass by; (figuratively) to pass for, to be taken for.

exercises.why: **выйти / выходить** — to exit, to go out; to appear, to be published; to spend, to be used up; to come off, to come out. — DLI, Lesson 79.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: Tom doesn't want to go out.
exercises.context: выйти / выходить — to exit, to go out; to appear, to be published; to spend, to be used up; to come off, to come out.

exercises.why: The imperfective aspect emphasizes the action itself. — From the DLI Grammar Reference Book, Lesson 37.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: The imperfective aspect emphasizes the action itself.

exercises.why: **перенести / переносить** — to transfer, to carry, to transport; (word) to carry over to the next line; to postpone, to put off; to extend. **привести / приводить** — to bring (someone with); to lead (of a road); to result, to lead, to bring; (mathematics) to reduce. **довести / доводить** — to lead, to take, to accompany (to), to bring (into); (cooking) to scald; to drive, to reduce, to bring, to carry. **завести / заводить** — to take, to bring, to lead; to get, to procure, to acquire, to buy; to establish, to set up, to found; to start. — DLI, Lesson 79.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: перенести / переносить — to transfer, to carry, to transport; (word) to carry over to the next line; to postpone, to put off; to extend.

exercises.why: The second actor (if mentioned) is always in the Instrumental case with the preposition "**с**": *Я не хочу встречаться с этим человеком.* Note that without "**-ся**" the verb **встречать** — **встретить** is used with the direct object in the Accusative case: *Вчера я встретил моего друга.* but: *Мы встретились на улице.* We already know that the verbs in "**-ся**" may be divided into several groups. Verbs which never occur without the ending "**-ся**": *Я боюсь вашего брата.* — From the DLI Grammar Reference Book, Lessons 66–67.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: The second actor (if mentioned) is always in the Instrumental case with the preposition "**с**": *Я не хочу встречаться с этим человеком.* Note that without "**-ся**" the verb **встречать** — **встретить** is used with the direct object in the Accusative…
